name: Argentina
greetingNote: One kiss on the cheek is standard between almost anyone, men included.

name: Australia
greetingNote: ‘G’day’ is real but informal; a handshake and first names are the norm.

name: Belgium
greetingNote: Language is political here — Dutch in Flanders, French in Wallonia. In Brussels, either.

name: Brazil
greetingNote: Warm and physical: expect a hug or cheek kisses rather than a handshake.

name: Belize
greetingNote: English is official and Spanish is spoken in most homes — either greeting lands well.

name: Canada
greetingNote: In Quebec, lead with Bonjour — it is genuinely appreciated.

name: Switzerland
greetingNote: Four national languages. German, French or Italian depending on the canton; try Grüezi in Zurich.

name: China
greetingNote: A slight nod and a handshake; skip the hug with someone you have just met.

name: Egypt
greetingNote: The reply to Assalamu alaikum is Wa alaikum assalam — peace upon you too.

name: Spain
greetingNote: Two cheek kisses, right cheek first, between women or a woman and a man.

name: France
greetingNote: Always open with Bonjour before anything else — skipping it reads as rude.

name: United Kingdom
greetingNote: A handshake or just a nod. In Wales try Shwmae, in Scotland Hullo.

name: Greenland
greetingNote: Danish is also widely spoken.

name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
Hong Kong
greetingNote: Cantonese, not Mandarin — Nei hou, not Ni hao.

name: India
greetingNote: Press your palms together at chest height as you say it; a handshake is also fine.

name: Iran
greetingNote: Salaam works for everyone. Do not offer a handshake to someone of the opposite sex unless they extend first.

name: Japan
greetingNote: A small bow rather than a handshake; deeper bow, more respect.

alsoTry.local: ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်

name: Mexico
greetingNote: A handshake, then a one-armed hug once you know someone.

name: Nigeria
greetingNote: Greetings are unhurried — ask after family before getting to the point.

name: New Zealand
greetingNote: Kia ora is Māori and used by nearly everyone, whatever their background.

name: Portugal
greetingNote: Say Bom dia before noon and Boa tarde after — Olá works any time.

name: Saudi Arabia
greetingNote: Men often greet with a handshake and a nose-touch between friends; follow their lead.

name: Thailand
greetingNote: Add the wai — palms together, a slight bow — and say it as Sawasdee krap (men) or ka (women).

name: Turkey
greetingNote: A firm handshake; among older men, a kiss on both cheeks.

name: United States
greetingNote: A handshake and first names, immediately.

name: South Africa
greetingNote: Eleven official languages. Sawubona is Zulu; Afrikaans speakers say Hallo, and English works everywhere.
